hooks.text: Giant clouds of glowing gas dwarf our entire galaxy.
Some single objects in space make our galaxy look tiny.
What deep space giants span four times our entire galaxy?

title: The Glowing Giants That Dwarf Our Galaxy
description: Deep in the early universe, enormous clouds of glowing hydrogen span hundreds of thousands of light-years. Astronomers solved the mystery of what powers these cosmic behemoths.

beats.text: Giant clouds of glowing gas dwarf our entire galaxy.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a massive glowing Lyman-alpha blob surrounding galaxies

beats.text: Astronomers in 2000 discovered hydrogen blobs spanning 400,000 light-years across.
beats.visual: Deep space observation image of glowing Lyman-alpha blob LAB-1

beats.text: Using the Subaru Telescope, team members found 30 more along a cosmic filament.
beats.visual: Photograph of Subaru Telescope dome on Mauna Kea at night
queries: Subaru Telescope summit Mauna Kea night

beats.text: Nothing that huge should shine so brightly billions of light-years away.
beats.visual: Computer simulation of the cosmic web showing massive filaments

beats.text: Scientists debated if gas was falling in or supernovas were blowing out.
beats.visual: Artist concept of supernova explosions blowing out galactic gas

beats.text: But polarized light proved the primary power was hidden inside.
beats.visual: Very Large Telescope array at Paranal Observatory at night

beats.text: Supermassive black holes inside act like cosmic lightbulbs, illuminating the gas.
beats.visual: Artist concept of an active galactic nucleus with supermassive black hole
queries: Supermassive black hole accretion disk illustration

beats.text: These hidden engines explain how giant gas clouds dwarf our galaxy.
beats.visual: Composite image comparing the Milky Way to a giant gas cloud
